scenario: A media-economics study observes only multilingual newsrooms that remain profitable, recording mean monthly unique visitors of 38M (σ=8M). The profitability survival threshold is 22M monthly visitors. Researchers need the true mean reach across all multilingual newsrooms that launched.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming monthly unique visitors is normally distributed with σ=8 million visitors, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>22]=38. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The multilingual newsrooms among those still profitable monthly unique visitors set is a truncated-normal sample above the 22 threshold. Solving E[X|X>22]=μ+σφ((22−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((22−μ)/σ)=38 gives μ≈37.49806. Only 97.4% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.5019 million visitors.

naive_answer: The true mean monthly unique visitors is 38 million visitors because that is the observed average among multilingual newsrooms among those still profitable.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=22. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=38. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈37.49806. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((22−37.49806)/σ)≈0.97364.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 38,8,22
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-37.49806)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.97364)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
